tasks.short: Approve people plans, assess senior candidates and decide major organisational changes.

steps.what: Compile staffing, leadership vacancy and budget information for the people proposal.
Read the people proposal and identify assumptions, trade-offs and missing evidence.

loop.input: People proposal, company strategy and organisation chart.
loop.output: Source-linked assumptions, unresolved questions and stated organisational trade-offs.
loop.check: Verify citations and financial figures against supplied records; executive reviews relevance and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unresolved points return to the HR director.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text proposals express dependencies and assumptions that fixed fields do not capture.

steps.what: Discuss staffing options, organisational consequences and implementation constraints with the leadership team.
Interview senior finalists and discuss leadership expectations when the proposal includes recruitment.
Approve the people plan, senior selection or organisational change within delegated authority.
Approve reserved appointments or structural changes when the board charter requires it.
Record authorised staffing changes and route implementation actions to their owners.

tasks.design: A deterministic integration assembles authorised staffing and budget facts from the {HCM}, {ATS} and {ERP}; a bounded reading loop prepares source-linked questions in the {DOCS}. Configure the {WORKFLOW} to route executive and reserved board approvals, then create only the authorised records and actions in the {HCM}, {ATS} and {PROJECT}. Leadership discussions, candidate assessment and organisational choices remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: People proposals combine confidential records, narrative assumptions and authority rules across several systems. Standard approvals do not resolve leadership judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building narrow data adapters and validation checks. Bounded document extraction can reduce preparation without selecting candidates or deciding structures.
tasks.still_hard: Leadership fit, organisational politics and consultation remain demanding. GDPR, applicable EU AI Act duties and national employment and consultation rules require purpose-specific assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Judge leadership potential, earn trust and accept responsibility for the consequences of organisational change.

ambition.what: Quarterly leadership-capacity review against funded strategic priorities.

tasks.altitude: The executive spends less time assembling evidence and more time testing organisational choices with department heads. No appointment or restructuring authority changes automatically; board reservations remain in force.

reach.task: Translate approved organisational changes into operating responsibilities and capacity plans.
reach.learn: Capacity modelling, role dependencies and consultation sequencing.

evidence.claim: Structured papers can be drafted from management documents with missing analysis flagged.
Staffing-data integration and approval routing are feasible with deterministic technology; executive judgement remains manual.
GDPR Article 22 limits solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
Certain employment-related AI uses are listed as high-risk; classification depends on intended use.

assumptions: Shares and remaining time are illustrative active effort across the listed roles, not measured executive savings.
The task mixes people planning, structural changes and senior selection; interviews and board approval are conditional.
Existing approval configuration can record authorised changes without custom write adapters.
Build ranges cover one pilot workflow; consultation and access can overlap other work.
unknowns: Which appointments and organisational changes require board approval?
Which national consultation rules and employee agreements apply?
Can the systems expose appropriately restricted staffing, candidate and budget records?
How much of the actual workload involves senior recruitment?
research_questions: Which existing approval features support conditional board routing and a complete decision history?
Would the precise proposed use fall within employment-related high-risk AI provisions?
new_work: Review extracted assumptions and missing evidence.
Resolve inconsistent staffing and budget records.
Maintain delegation rules and access restrictions.
Check that implementation actions match the approved decision.

tasks.short: Appoint managers and agree their responsibilities, authority and working relationships.

steps.what: Check the selected appointment, reporting line and existing responsibilities.
Draft the manager's mandate, expected outcomes and limits of authority.

loop.input: Approved appointment context, strategy and delegation policy.
loop.output: Draft mandate with outcomes, reporting relationships and explicit authority limits.
loop.check: Validate names and authority limits against records; executive reviews objectives and unresolved overlaps.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing authority stays blank for human resolution.
loop.why_not_simpler: Situation-specific objectives and responsibility descriptions require prose beyond a fixed template.

steps.what: Discuss the mandate, resources and responsibility overlaps with the manager and affected peers.
Authorise the appointment and delegated responsibilities within the approved governance framework.
Update the manager record, reporting line and approved responsibility register.
Confirm ownership, handover arrangements and escalation expectations with the appointed manager.

tasks.design: Configure an appointment view in the {HCM} and a mandate template in the {DOCS}; a bounded drafting loop fills narrative sections from approved context. Human agreement and authorisation release a configured {WORKFLOW} that updates the {HCM} and responsibility register. The solution records delegation without allocating work through inferred employee traits.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appointment records are structured, but mandates and peer boundaries are negotiated in conversation and recorded inconsistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record and approval features handle most administration. A small drafting loop can turn approved context into a reviewable mandate.
tasks.still_hard: Real authority depends on trust, resources and cooperation across departments. Contract changes, GDPR, EU AI Act scope and national consultation requirements need assessment for the actual use.
tasks.human_edge: Choose whom to trust, negotiate workable authority and secure commitment from affected managers.

ambition.what: Monthly resolution of cross-department decision bottlenecks.

tasks.altitude: The executive spends less time reconstructing mandates and more time resolving contested responsibilities. Decision rights change only through an explicit approved delegation.

reach.task: Resolve operational handover gaps between departments.
reach.learn: Decision-right mapping, escalation design and resource negotiation.

evidence.claim: Appointment records, responsibility registers and approval routing can use existing software configuration.
A bounded drafting loop can prepare mandates while people retain appointment and delegation decisions.
AI used for certain employment decisions or task allocation based on personal traits is listed as high-risk.

assumptions: Shares and remaining time are planning estimates across the listed participants.
Candidate selection and any reserved board approval precede appointment implementation.
The existing systems support a configurable appointment view and approved-record updates.
The scope excludes individual performance scoring and automatic task allocation.
Consultation and access ranges include national requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Where are delegation limits and responsibility records maintained?
Which appointments require contractual changes or further approval?
Can configured workflows update reporting lines with a reliable audit history?
Which affected employee representatives must be consulted?
research_questions: Can existing configuration version mandates and show conflicting responsibility assignments?
Which clauses and authority limits can be validated deterministically?
new_work: Review mandate drafts for unsupported objectives or authority.
Maintain mandate templates and delegation limits.
Handle failed record updates and incomplete handovers.

tasks.short: Interpret policies and laws, resolve ambiguity and explain their practical implications.

steps.what: Receive the question and clarify its audience, facts and required response.
Locate current policies, relevant legal texts and previously approved interpretations.
Read the sources and form an interpretation for the specific situation.

loop.input: Scoped question and dated, jurisdiction-tagged policy source pack.
loop.output: Draft explanation with passage references, assumptions and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Check every citation against supplied text; executive reviews applicability and counsel handles ambiguity.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; absent or conflicting authority produces an unresolved question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Applying free-text rules to a particular situation requires contextual interpretation.

steps.what: Resolve legal ambiguity and agree the interpretation to communicate.
Explain the interpretation, practical consequences and limits to the audience.
Send a written explanation with sources, qualifications and agreed follow-up.

loop.input: Reviewed interpretation, audience description and agreed follow-up.
loop.output: Plain-language written explanation preserving sources and qualifications.
loop.check: Compare claims with the reviewed interpretation; executive approves wording and recipient before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; new substantive questions return to legal counsel.
loop.why_not_simpler: Audience-specific explanation needs prose while preserving nuanced qualifications.

tasks.design: Configure a question form in the {WORKFLOW} and searchable, dated source records in the {DOCS}, with approved references to the {GOV_PORTAL}. A bounded answer desk drafts source-linked interpretations for executive and legal review; a second bounded pass prepares the written explanation in the {EMAIL}. Sending requires approval, while nuanced explanations remain human conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions arrive without essential context, and applicable sources are scattered across versions and jurisdictions. Search alone cannot establish the right interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata filters and versioned source registers improve retrieval. Bounded drafting can produce a checkable explanation from a restricted source pack.
tasks.still_hard: A correct quotation can still support an incorrect interpretation. Legal judgement, changing national rules, GDPR-sensitive facts and applicable EU AI Act obligations remain material.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the audience's real concern, explain uncertainty and take responsibility for the organisation's position.

ambition.what: Reviewed policy-change briefings for department heads.

tasks.altitude: The executive prepares explanations faster and can spend more time discussing consequences with department heads. Legal interpretation and authority to commit the organisation remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate a reviewed policy change into operating procedures.
reach.learn: Source traceability, policy exceptions and the distinction between legal requirements and company choices.

evidence.claim: A source-referenced answer tool supports staff answering planning-rule questions with human checking.
Fabricated references and a fabricated court case were reported in an AI-assisted government report.
AI-generated public-interest text has transparency provisions, including an exception involving human review and editorial responsibility.
Metadata-based source retrieval and scoped intake can be implemented without a model.

assumptions: Shares and remaining time are estimates for substantive questions, not routine policy lookups.
Legal counsel may be internal or external and is available for material ambiguity.
The source register supports deterministic retrieval by topic, jurisdiction and effective date.
Source selection remains reviewed; the system does not claim exhaustive legal research.
The example ends with an external response; internal questions follow the same preparation path.
unknowns: Which policy topics and jurisdictions dominate the workload?
Who approves legal interpretations and external organisational positions?
Are source documents current, searchable and licensed for this use?
Does the intended rollout require employee consultation under national rules?
Will explanations be private replies or public-interest publications?
research_questions: How reliably can source revisions and effective dates be detected?
Which question types can reuse an approved explanation without new interpretation?
What retrieval coverage is sufficient for the initial policy domain?
new_work: Maintain the source register and remove superseded interpretations.
Review citations, applicability and preserved qualifications.
Handle missing facts and conflicting sources.
Return substantive follow-up questions to legal counsel.
Assess publication disclosure requirements where applicable.

tasks.short: Review staff reports, challenge conclusions and approve recommendations or request changes.

steps.what: Collect emailed report attachments and chase the current versions.
Check report figures against financial and operating records and reconcile differences.
Read reports, compare results with plans and identify questions or unsupported conclusions.

loop.input: Versioned reports, reconciled figures, explicit exceptions and approved plan.
loop.output: Source-linked changes, unsupported claims and suggested questions for the executive.
loop.check: Validate all cited figures and calculations deterministically; executive checks significance and reads flagged passages.
loop.stop: One analysis and one correction pass; unresolved data conflicts remain visible and receive no inferred answer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative claims and omitted reasoning require reading beyond numeric variance thresholds.

steps.what: Challenge assumptions and discuss proposed changes with the report owner.
Approve the recommendation, reject it or specify required revisions.
Record the decision and create agreed actions, owners and due dates.

tasks.design: Replace attachment collection with scheduled submissions to the {DOCS}, then reconcile approved extracts from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A {BI} view shows checked variances while a bounded loop drafts source-linked review questions. After the executive records a decision, configured automation creates the agreed actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports arrive in inconsistent versions, measures differ between departments and reconciliations live in separate workbooks. Summarisation cannot repair those foundations.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes narrow connectors and metric checks cheaper to build. Bounded reading adds narrative challenge once the underlying data is reconciled.
tasks.still_hard: Metric ownership, weak source data and strategically misleading narratives remain difficult. Employee-level reporting may bring GDPR, EU AI Act and national consultation obligations beyond this aggregate-reporting scope.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what a report leaves unsaid, challenge the owner constructively and decide which risks deserve action.

ambition.what: Fortnightly review of emerging operating risks.

tasks.altitude: The executive spends less time finding versions and checking arithmetic, and more time challenging recommendations. Approval authority remains unchanged; faster evidence can support more frequent risk discussions.

reach.task: Investigate operating exceptions and turn executive decisions into corrective actions.
reach.learn: Metric lineage, variance diagnosis and action-effectiveness review.

evidence.claim: Report summarisation and data questions are supported today, with data preparation affecting answer quality.
A vendor case reports executive-reporting time savings; its method is not supplied in the digest.
Management-document tools can flag missing forward-looking analysis in structured papers.
Versioned submission, numeric reconciliation and action creation can be deterministic; proposed time reductions are estimates.

assumptions: Shares and remaining time are estimates across the listed participants, not documented savings.
The pilot covers recurring aggregate operating and financial reports.
Direct submission removes attachment collection, while report owners still produce and submit their reports.
Source records have usable identifiers, periods and agreed metric definitions.
Configured action creation requires explicit owners and dates in the approved decision.
unknowns: Which reports actually require executive approval rather than acknowledgement?
How much review time concerns data quality versus strategic judgement?
Are financial and operating metrics defined consistently?
Which extracts, interfaces and access permissions are available?
Do any reports contain employee monitoring or individual performance data?
research_questions: Which existing submission and approval features can remove attachment chasing?
What reconciliation coverage is achievable before changing source data models?
How should the review brief expose missing evidence without creating excessive false alarms?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation exceptions and refresh failures.
Maintain metric definitions, thresholds and source mappings.
Review narrative claims and cited evidence.
Handle incomplete decisions before creating actions.
Periodically check whether review questions improve decisions.

role.altitude: The chief executive's week shifts modestly from evidence assembly and paperwork toward leadership conversations, organisational trade-offs and operating-risk decisions. Appointment, legal-position and strategic approval rights remain governed by existing delegations and board reservations.
reach: Work with the general and operations manager on capacity constraints and department boundaries.
Connect reviewed policy changes to operating procedures and exception routes.
Use reconciled reporting to investigate emerging risks and assess corrective actions.
skills_to_grow: Define decision rights and escalation limits precisely.
Distinguish source-supported facts from interpretations and assumptions.
Challenge metric definitions and understand data lineage.
Evaluate bounded model outputs without delegating accountability.
Negotiate mandates and organisational change with affected people.
role.ambitious_version: Run a regular leadership-capacity and operating-risk review using consistent evidence, then resolve cross-department constraints before they become major delivery failures. This requires explicit agreement on review cadence and delegated authority.
